jobs.title: Defense Engines AI Transformation Leader
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Transform engine and spare-part delivery for Defense Engines & Services (DES). This role owns the product vision, roadmap, and end-to-end lifecycle for the data, analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) capability that makes that transformation possible. Act as the customer representative for a portfolio of interdependent products spanning new engine production and Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO), from demand and forecast through fulfillment and service and support. Success is measured through DES KPIs, led by on-time delivery and spare-part output, then inventory and net productivity.

This is a forward-deployed role. You will work alongside the planners, operators, and engineers who own the delivery, and you will build digital capability with them, taking AI-enabled ideas from concept to medium and high-fidelity working prototypes on real production data.

Job Description
This role will also require in-person attendance for New Hire Orientation on Day 1

Roles and Responsibilities
In this role, you will:
- Own all aspects of the lifecycle (planning, forecasting, production) for multiple interdependent data, analytics, and AI products that together form the DES delivery transformation program and represent the customer in every scope and sequencing tradeoff.

- Build and maintain the DES data and analytics product roadmap, sequence it against the constraints that actually limit engine and spare-part output, and identify and secure the stakeholders needed to support it.

- Stand up self-service data and analytics on manufacturing, quality, and delivery data so planners, buyers, and shop leaders answer their own questions in the moment rather than opening a DT ticket. This closes the single largest capability gap in the portfolio.

- Operationalize and sustain value from advanced analytics and agentic AI investments, and move proven prototypes inside the operating model rather than leaving them adjacent to it, where they stay advisory.

- Partner with central DT and Enterprise Data on data fabric and ontology adoption so DES manufacturing, quality, and delivery data is modeled once and reused across products.

- Take AI-enabled ideas from concept to working software. Build low-fidelity proofs to test feasibility, then advance the survivors to medium and high-fidelity prototypes on real production data, in the hands of real users, and decide quickly which ones earn production investment and which get killed.

- Work forward-deployed. Embed with operators, planners, and engineers at the Genba, build with them rather than collecting requirements and handing them off, and stay on the problem until the capability is in use.

- Use rapid prototyping as a countermeasure inside Daily Management, converting Key Performance Indicator (KPI) and Targets to Improve (TTI) gaps into working capability in weeks rather than quarters.

- Define the value case in delivery terms up front (engine days, turnaround time, schedule adherence, inventory turns, cost), drive early materialization of benefits, and report outcomes against the 2026 DES measures. Stop or redirect work that does not move a delivery number.

- Influence Executive Band (EB) leaders and below on investment decisions, and partner with business, finance, and DT leadership to align Digital Technology spend with value stream priorities.

- Set data and AI standards across the DES horizontal so use, implementation, support, and technical integrity stay consistent and do not fragment by product line.

- Operate as a player-coach. Mentor product managers and engineers on systems thinking for large-scale problems, lean and experimental product practice, and raise the team's data and AI fluency.

- Manage supplier and contractor partners delivering analytics and AI work, hold them to outcomes, and reduce the team's dependence on expensive external delivery.

- Lead risk management for the portfolio, including export control, cybersecurity, data governance, and responsible AI, and design controls into products instead of relying on exception processes.

Business Acumen
- Translates business problems into product bets, quantifies the value, and makes tradeoffs across a multi-product portfolio based on business priority rather than the loudest request.

- Establishes performance metrics and drives continuous improvement across systems, processes, and resources.

- Demonstrated customer focus; evaluates decisions through the eyes of the operator on the floor and partners with the business to shape future initiatives.

- Decomposes problems and decides when the problem or the solution is not fully defined.

- Constructs multiyear scenarios for data-centric methods and technologies under uncertainty, and interprets industry trends that should inform the roadmap.

Leadership
- Sets and changes direction at the enterprise level by building direct and indirect support for ideas, largely without formal authority.

- Leads and influences across a complex matrix organization, including Executive Band leaders and their teams, and incorporates stakeholder input while still deciding.

- Directs and mentors others toward a systems thinking approach for solving large-scale problems, and removes roadblocks on behalf of the team.

- Owns decisions, including outcomes and any required rework plans.

- Acts as a catalyst for change, rewards early adopters, and builds a culture of proactive problem solving rather than reactive break-fix.

Personal Attributes
- Excellent written and oral communication; presents concise facts and the implications of alternatives in a way that is relevant to senior leadership and customers.
- Strategic thinker who converts vision into a concrete action plan with named owners and dates.

- Manages uncertainty for self and others, and makes confident decisions when problems or solutions are not 100% defined.

- Curious and creative; removes barriers to the creativity of others and pushes simplicity and speed.

- Biased toward demonstration over documentation. Would rather show a working prototype than present a plan for one.

- Strong analytical, project management, and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize under pressure and tight deadlines.

Required Qualification
Bachelor’s degree from accredited university or college with minimum of 10 years of professional experience OR Associates degree with minimum of 13 years of professional experience OR High School Diploma with minimum of 15 years of professional experience
Minimum 8 years of professional experience in IT
Note: Military experience is equivalent to professional experience
Ability to travel; 10-50%

Eligibility Requirement:
-Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required.  We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job.

Desired Qualification
Technical Expertise
- Hands-on builder with a forward-deployed engineering mindset. Personally produces working artifacts (data pipelines, ontology and semantic models, notebooks, agent workflows, and functional user interfaces) rather than only specifying them, and is fluent in Python, SQL, or equivalent.

- Demonstrated ability to move an idea across fidelity levels under time pressure: proof of concept to prove feasibility, medium fidelity to prove the workflow, high fidelity to prove production readiness and earn investment.

- Demonstrated ownership of data platform and advanced analytics products at scale, covering ingestion, modeling, governance, performance, and self-service consumption.

- Working fluency with modern analytics and AI, including machine learning, large language model, retrieval, and agentic patterns, and the judgment to know where those methods do not belong.

- Working knowledge of manufacturing and MRO data and systems, including Manufacturing Execution System (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), quality, and shop-floor technology, and how that data becomes a delivery or inventory decision.

- Deep technology, process, and domain expertise sufficient to influence product design whether the product is built internally or bought.

- Strong track record of understanding current and emerging technologies, demonstrated through training, job experience, or industry activities.

- Demonstrated understanding of Lean Six Sigma principles (for example, Green Belt certified) and comfort operating inside a Daily Management system.

The base pay range for this position is $176,000 - $235,000 annually. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 6th, 2026.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Strategic Packaging
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military aircraft. You’ll be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives. Most importantly, you’ll share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!
GE Aerospace is undertaking a major, business-wide transformation as it relates to our packaging portfolio and the emerging regulatory landscape, most notably the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation and California SB 54. These requirements will impact packaging design, materials, recyclability, reporting, and extended producer responsibility across all products, sites, and channels.
We are seeking a Program Manager for Strategic Packaging with strong program and project management capability, deep packaging design and materials expertise, and continuous improvement experience. This role will lead the global packaging transformation program end-to-end, providing the technical depth needed to guide and challenge packaging solutions so they are compliant, safe, operationally efficient, and cost-effective.

Job Description
Key Responsibilities
- Lead the global Strategic Packaging Program. Define scope, roadmap, milestones, dependencies, and governance. Run steering forums, manage risks/issues, and ensure alignment across businesses and regions.
- Translate global regulatory requirements into a coherent packaging transformation strategy and implementation plan.
- In partnership with product/quality teams, guide the development of compliant packaging designs and global standards. Ensure new specifications (materials, structures, recyclability criteria, test protocols) protect product integrity, safety, and customer experience while meeting regulatory thresholds.
- Coordinate design, validation, and rollout of packaging changes across manufacturing, MRO, spares distribution, and logistics. Collaborate with suppliers to implement new packaging standards, support trials and qualifications, and resolve technical and operational issues.
- Drive continuous improvement in packaging: material reduction, cube and freight optimization, standardization of packaging families, increased use of reusables and recyclable content, and reduction of total landed cost.
- Lead change management for the packaging transformation. Assess impacts by product, site, and role; develop communication and training plans; coordinate training content with packaging and operations experts; and ensure new packaging standards are understood, adopted, and sustained at sites and with suppliers.
- Define and track key program KPIs, including compliance status by market/product, packaging material mix and recyclability, EPR and fee impacts, damage/quality metrics, and cost performance. Provide regular updates to senior leadership and support external reporting needs as required.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university in Packaging Engineering, Mechanical/Industrial Engineering, Materials Science, Supply Chain, or related field; advanced degree or PMP/Prince2 a plus (or a high school diploma/GED with a minimum of 4 years packaging, product engineering, supply chain/logistics, or operations experience)
- Minimum 5 years of experience in program/project management or transformation roles.
- Demonstrated experience with packaging design and validation (materials, structural design, cushioning, testing) in a manufacturing or distribution environment.
- Familiarity with packaging-related regulatory requirements (preferably EU packaging/PPWR, EPR schemes, and/or US state-level packaging regulations).
- Proven ability to lead cross-functional, multi-site or multi-region programs, managing scope, schedule, risks, and stakeholders.
- Proficiency with project tools (e.g., MS Project/Smartsheet), data/analytics (Excel, SQL/BI a plus), and process mapping.
- Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and vendor negotiation skills.

Desired Qualifications
- Experience in aerospace, automotive, industrial, or similarly high-value and regulated industries.
- Prior involvement in programs addressing sustainability, circularity, or extended producer responsibility.
- Familiarity with logistics operations and systems (ERP, WMS, TMS) and how packaging affects storage, handling, and transport.
- Exposure to continuous improvement/lean methods applied to packaging, logistics, or manufacturing.

Competencies
- Strategic planning and execution
- Risk management and issue resolution
- Technical credibility
- Systems integration and data readiness
- Compliance- and risk-aware
- Customer- and quality-focused
- Data-driven and improvement-oriented
- Clear, concise communication

jobs.title: Program Manager - Directorate of Defense Trade Controls Consent Agreement
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
GE Aerospace is seeking a Program Manager - DDTC Consent Agreement to lead the execution of key workstreams supporting the company’s trade compliance obligations under its Consent Agreement with the U.S. Department of State’s Directorate of Defense Trade Controls (DDTC). This role is responsible for planning, coordinating, tracking, and reporting program activities to ensure commitments, milestones, corrective actions, and reporting requirements are completed accurately and on time.

Reporting to the Executive Leader, International Trade Compliance and partnering closely with the Chief Counsel for Regulatory Affairs, the Program Manager will work across Legal & Compliance, business teams, and other functional stakeholders to drive alignment, accountability, and timely execution. The ideal candidate is a strong program leader who can manage multiple complex initiatives in a matrixed and highly regulated environment. Prior International Trade Compliance experience is not required; however, experience in compliance, legal, or other regulated settings is preferred.

Job Description
Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead program management for execution of the   DDTC Consent Agreement, including integrated planning, milestone tracking, risk management, and closure of actions across multiple workstreams.
- Plan and manage regular operating cadences, including weekly meetings, and partner with workstream owners to ensure commitments and milestones are delivered on time in alignment with Consent Agreement requirements and Special Compliance Officer (SCO) expectations.
- Coordinate engagement with internal leaders and external stakeholders, as needed, including the   Special Compliance Officer, external auditor, and DDTC.
- Prepare executive-level status reports and briefing materials summarizing program progress, key risks, action items, resource needs, and overall performance against commitments.
- Drive cross-functional execution of Consent Agreement requirements, including support for audits, digital transformation initiatives, training, and jurisdiction/classification validation activities.
- Monitor, track, and escalate program risks, issues, and remediation actions, ensuring clear ownership, due dates, and completion criteria.
- Support the development and continuous improvement of processes, procedures, training, and governance mechanisms needed to sustain compliance commitments.
- Apply   lean and process improvement   principles to strengthen program execution, action tracking, reporting, and operating rhythms.
- Lead effectively in ambiguous or evolving situations, balancing long-term strategic priorities with urgent tactical actions and deadlines.

Required Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree from accredited university or college with minimum of 10 years of professional experience in compliance, legal or other regulated settings OR Associates degree with minimum of 12 years of professional experience compliance, legal or other regulated settings OR High School Diploma with minimum of 14 years of professional experience compliance, legal or other regulated settings
- Minimum 8 years of professional experience in compliance, legal or other regulated settings

​
Desired Characteristics
- Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives and driving multiple workstreams to completion.
- Strong experience with integrated planning, status reporting, executive communications, and stakeholder management.
- Ability to work effectively across a matrixed organization and influence stakeholders without direct authority.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, including the ability to interpret, analyze, and synthesize data into actions and decisions.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of clear materials for senior leadership.
- Experience in a regulated, compliance-driven, legal, audit, or risk management environment, including support for compliance transformation, governance, remediation programs, and regulatory commitments.
- Familiarity with lean methodologies, process optimization, and structured operating cadences.
- Experience creating and managing executive-level reporting and presentations.
- Excellent communicator with strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
- Proven ability to identify, analyze, and solve ambiguous problems with strong attention to detail.
- Proactive, can-do mindset with a focus on continuous improvement.

The base pay range for this position is $181,000 - $241,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan.  This posting is expected to close on September 18th, 2026.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Whether you want to work at one of our facilities as the site leader's right hand helping to make business decisions or at headquarters on a larger finance team, we have an opportunity for you. You’ll get to work with budgets of various sizes and complexities, while collaborating with others. Our finance and accounting teams span the globe, providing unmatched learning, development, and career growth opportunities.

The Senior Finance Manager is a critical position on the Rutland Integrated Manufacturing Leadership team. This position requires a strategic thinker with a deep level of financial expertise and an ability to partner with Operational Leadership to achieve business outcomes. This position drives optimal performance of safety, quality, delivery & cost at the site and contributes to the overall Company performance. The successful candidate will manage $200M+ of cost, drive productivity, improve financial reporting and analysis, and oversee significant capital investments ensuring alignment with GE Aerospace’s strategic priorities.

Seasoned, senior level individual contributor requiring in-depth understanding of their business, function and how their role integrates with others within their discipline. Role requires good understanding of customers, industry and functions.

Job Description
Job Description and Responsibilities

Rutland financial leadership - deliver accurate and complete financials, including financial planning, forecasting, variance analysis, month-end closing activities, and ad-hoc analytics to drive operational action

Strategic partnership with Rutland Site Leader and operations team (Site Leadership)
- Collaborate with Site Leadership to ensure alignment and execution of key priorities

- Partner with cost leader to drive operations team to meet the site’s year-over-year productivity targets

- Proactively provide unsolicited guidance, interpretation, and education of complex financial and operational matters to drive business decisions

Maximize ROI on a $35M+ annual capital expenditure budget, ensuring investments deliver measurable value to the business

Develop Budget/Forecasts and achieve financial results in a dynamic environment, ensuring the Site meets its financial and operational targets

Implement GE proprietary lean operating system (FLIGHT DECK) to drive business and financial results for safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC)

Effectively communicate key dynamics of the site operations to Site Leadership, Part Family Leadership, and FP&A along with other cross-divisional and cross-functional internal stakeholders

Maintain the highest standards of controllership, compliance & rigor
- Ensure compliance to GAAP and GE policy to ensure reporting integrity, partnering consistently and effectively with controllership, FP&A, engineering & the Commercial Engines and Services/Defense teams

- Own the annual Government reporting process (FPRP) and support any Government audits if required

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university (CPA, CMA or MBA a plus)

- 8+ years of relevant finance experience

- Prior experience working in supply chain at a mid to large size manufacturing environment

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

- Strong communication skills

- Demonstrated ability to identify, analyze, and resolve problems

- Work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment

Desired Qualifications
- Lean operating model experience

- Strong project management skills

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Integrated Manufacturing Assembly & Test FP&A Leader manages planning, analysis, and reporting for the consolidated view of Part Families and IMAT as an aggregate. This leader should support the Integrated Manufacturing Assembly & Test CFO by enabling IMAT-wide standard work and efficient financial processes. This role will provide strategic financial insights and support decision-making processes. This leader will work directly with the entire IMAT General Manager and IMAT Staff to enable operational performance and implement strategies that align with business objectives.

In addition to FP&A responsibilities, a critical part of this role is directly supporting special projects across the IMAT Shops, including, but not limited to Business Development opportunities, key acquisition integrations, ERP implementation projects, and various other IMAT-level strategic initiatives. This role will be responsible for leading and managing key efforts in these special projects to support the IMAT division.

Job Description
Roles and Responsibilities
As the Integrated Manufacturing Assembly & Test FP&A leader you will:
- Financial Planning, Reporting, and Analysis : Lead Part Family and Shop finance teams in executing planning and reporting cycles, delivering comprehensive financial reports with variance analysis, and driving process automation to enhance transparency and streamline reporting.
- Forecasting and Risk Management : Manage planning, forecasting, and pacing activities by leveraging data insights and operational expertise to identify material variances, mitigate risks, and capitalize on opportunities, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial results.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration and Communication : Foster engagement with cross-functional teams to effectively communicate financial positions, analyze operating results, and provide actionable insights to support strategic decision-making.
- Operational Reviews and Consolidation : Own the consolidation and analysis of financial data for IMAT’s Monthly Operating Reviews (MORs) and Weekly Operating Reviews (WORs), ensuring alignment with organizational goals and priorities.
- Strategic Planning and Reporting : Lead planning, forecasting, and pacing efforts for IMAT HQ, utilizing data-driven approaches to articulate material variances, risks, and opportunities. Support the IMAT CFO in preparing presentations and materials for key reviews, including MORs, WORs, Wrap Reviews, Budget, Strategy, and Board of Directors meetings.
- Continuous Improvement Through FLIGHT DECK : Apply FLIGHT DECK methodologies to drive continuous improvement across all financial processes within IMAT, fostering a lean and efficient operating model.
- Special Projects and Strategic Initiatives : Collaborate across shops and part families to lead or support special projects, including developing business cases, conducting due diligence for business development, integrating new sites and ERPs, and spearheading IM-level cross-functional initiatives.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in finance or accounting from an accredited university
- 6+ years of FP&A/Supply Chain Finance experience

Desired Characteristics
- Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
- Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects cross-functionally
- Experience with shop/supply chain finance
- Proven track record of driving financial performance
- Evidence of leveraging FLIGHT DECK to improve processes
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex financial data and provide actionable insights.
- Strong business acumen and strategic thinking capabilities.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
- High level of integrity, professionalism, and attention to detail.

jobs.title: GE Aerospace Programme Management - 12 Month Placement
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
In the 12- month Programme Management Placement, the successful candidate will join our Customer Programmes team which supports civil and military customers of our propeller systems for airborne and amphibious applications.

Job Description
About GE Aerospace

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we are advancing aviation technologies for today and tomorrow. Your work will contribute to the production of advanced jet engines, components, and integrated systems that power commercial and military   aircraft .   You’ll   be part of a team that embraces your drive, your curiosity, and your unique ideas and perspectives .    Most importantly,   you’ll   share in our pride and purpose that affects the lives of millions around the world!

Roles and Responsibilities

In the 12-month   Programme Man a gement   Placement offers diverse roles within the function, with responsibilities tailored to the specific needs of different teams. While all roles focus on program management, customer support, and operational efficiency, tasks will vary based on team priorities and projects.

Responsibilities may include:

- Coordinating customer requests such as RFQs and purchase orders, ensuring deadlines are met through collaboration with supply chain and engineering teams, preparing customer order books,   facilitating   client calls, and ensuring high satisfaction and   timely   delivery.

- Support Program Management Reviews (PMRs) by managing calendars, preparing agendas, and tracking actions.

- Leading process improvement projects to enhance operational efficiency, implementing Lean principles, and analysing operational data to create performance metrics that drive team focus on strategic priorities.

- Cross-functional collaboration is a key aspect of the role, working closely with Operations, Sourcing, Engineering, and Quality teams to meet customer and business   objectives . Some teams may focus on facilities and maintenance, including asset reviews, day-to-day operations, contractor control, and long-term projects to support stakeholders.

We have opportunities within:

- Field Services   (Dowty)   - managing   internal metrics, financials, materials, pricing models, and   logistics , with broad exposure to satellite sites and international field locations. The role involves tracking KPIs (such as turnaround times, schedule adherence, utilisation, and cost performance),   maintaining   dashboards and reports, and supporting root cause analysis of performance issues. You will   assist   with financial tracking (revenue, costs, margins), support pricing model updates, help manage materials data, and contribute to cost analysis for continuous improvement. On the operational side, you will coordinate   logistics   information, support planning for field   activities, and   maintain   documentation so stakeholders stay informed. The role requires close collaboration with Programmes, Finance, Operations, and Logistics, including supporting cross-functional reviews and small improvement projects in reporting, data quality, and process flow. The placement offers end-to-end exposure to field service operations, practical experience in metrics, financial and   logistics   coordination, and development of professional communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.

- Facilitates & Maintenance Projects   (Caledonian) - learning maintenance management and continuous improvement in a business operations environment, covering preventive and reactive maintenance, preventive maintenance planning, compliance, sustainability projects, and environmental monitoring and gap analysis. Monitoring performance metrics,   identifying   improvement opportunities and developing project management skills through small- to medium-scale projects. The role requires adapting to different people and environments daily, understanding departmental challenges to set maintenance priorities, communicating with various   stakeholders   and responding to critical needs, and learning from experienced staff to improve existing processes and work-scopes. Also working with suppliers and contractors during preventive maintenance to ensure high safety standards, gain exposure to shift supervision and maintenance management, and collaborate with internal and external resources on sustainment and environmental improvement projects.

- Military Platforms   (Cheltenham) - broad range of program management, customer support, order management, and cross-functional business improvement activities within a military-focused organisation. The role is designed to give the intern practical experience in managing internal special projects, supporting customer engagement, and becoming familiar with program management practices, procedures, internal systems, and standard work. The placement will work closely with stakeholders, customers, and colleagues across multiple functions, while contributing to business-focused projects, driving actions to closure, presenting findings and recommendations, and developing communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

- BizJet   Portfolio   (Cheltenham) - you will gain exposure to the complete program and product lifecycle, from new product introduction through to repair and overhaul services. The programs team you will join is a dynamic and growing portfolio, offering a strong opportunity to contribute to   day ‑ to ‑ day   program activities and develop core program management skills. Key activities include reviewing customer purchase orders and supporting the Program Team in managing the product orderbook, ensuring alignment between customer portals and internal order management systems. You will support sales and operational review meetings through orderbook management and engagement with key stakeholders involved in demand changes. You will help with obsolescence management by developing regular reviews with key functions,   monitoring   stock   run ‑ out   dates, and improving communication with other programs where obsolescence risk is shared. You will act as a “voice of the customer ”,   supporting communication between internal teams and the customer, engaging with customers to help secure invoice payment in support of cash targets, and helping to organise and support program review meetings with customers.

- OE Value Stream Programs   (Dowty)   - focuses   on planning, coordinating, and delivering manufactured spare   parts to   ensure reliable aftermarket support. The role owns the integrated production and delivery plan for defined part families, aligning production and materials with customer demand and business priorities, and applying a structured operating model to meet Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost   objectives . Working   cross ‑ functionally   with materials planning, manufacturing, quality, sourcing,   logistics , and   customer ‑ facing   teams, the role manages production schedules, monitors   performance, addresses risks and issues, and keeps customers informed through clear, proactive communication on delivery status, changes, and recovery plans. It combines operational planning,   data ‑ driven   performance management, and customer relationship management to improve delivery reliability and overall supply chain effectiveness.

- Programme Management Office   (Cheltenham)   - supporting the successful delivery of complex projects from early bid and concept stages through to closure. The PMO Project Controller   is responsible for   managing budgets and schedules using standardised tools,   maintaining   integrated project plans, and providing analysis to   identify   and mitigate cost and schedule risks. The role serves as a key point of contact for project management tools and practices, coaching project and technical leaders and performing earned value analysis to support informed decision-making. It also supports structured change and risk management processes, including preparing change documentation,   participating   in risk and opportunity reviews, and ensuring decisions are clearly recorded. In addition, the PMO Project Controller contributes to   accurate   project forecasting and helps coordinate resource plans across multiple teams to ensure projects are appropriately staffed and controlled.

- Programme Management  (Cheltenham) - This role offers a strong development opportunity in program management best practices by applying daily management and lean principles across all workstreams of one of our programmes. The individual will   be responsible for   maintaining   robust document control across NPI, production execution and aftermarket, coordinating actions with the integrated program team (IPT) following tollgate reviews and key meetings, and ensuring all program risks and opportunities are captured and managed in the digital thread tool. The role also includes monitoring and reporting touch labour and material performance against targets,   identifying   opportunities to eliminate   non ‑ value ‑ added   work using lean principles and project management principles. Through these activities, the individual will gain hands-on experience in quality assurance, QMS, risk management, and end-to-end program execution.

You will be guided by structured goals and   objectives   and will have responsibility to deliver on inspiring projects supported by your People Leader and team around you. We will guide you throughout the year to ensure you make the best of your GE Aerospace experience. Your People Leader will offer coaching and mentoring, and you will be provided with the opportunity to connect with other placement students across the UK.

This opportunity is offered in our   Caledonian (Prestwick, Scotland), Cheltenham, and   Gloucester (Dowty, a GE Aerospace company) sites ,   during the process we will ask you to share your location preferences.

GE Aerospace Caledonian   is a purpose-built   aircraft   engine overhaul facility,   adjacent to   Glasgow Prestwick International Airport. The Caledonian site was officially opened in 1980 and has since grown into a centre of excellence for Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) of CF6 &   GEnx   engine types. After each overhaul, the engines undergo intensive performance testing on site in our bespoke test cell, before returning to our global customer base ready for service.

Our vastly experienced and innovative workforce are passionate in the contribution towards the training of future engineers,   leaders   and surrounding talent in our organisation. At GE Caledonian, our Apprentices (Foundation, Modern & Graduate), XLP, OMLP and interns are key members of our team helping achieve the challenges of tomorrow. They continuously develop   new skills to keep up with the pace of change in the Aviation Industry and become comfortable working in this ever-challenging environment which thrives on embracing change.

Our diverse team have a strong foothold in the local community, proactively seeking new volunteering opportunities to give back and deliver on our corporate responsibility. We have a dedicated affinity group on site who   facilitate   opportunities to the wider team, creating an inclusive culture we can all be proud of.

With over 1,700 employees,   GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham   is one of the largest sites outside the USA and a major contributor to the local economy.

Our heritage   dates back to   1940 yet our technology is   cutting-edge . Located in the heart of Gloucestershire, the Power Distribution & Controls (PD&C) site focuses on the design, development and manufacture of   state-of-the-art   aircraft   power distribution and avionics systems for the global aviation industry. Our customers include all major aerospace manufacturers - covering commercial, business jet and military applications. The scale and complexity of engineering projects offer our employees unique opportunities to work on major international projects, developing critical   aircraft   systems that will be relied on by many people for decades to come.

At GE Aerospace we strive to be an employer of choice by offering internships, apprenticeships,   mentoring   and staff development programmes that create a workplace where everyone can be themselves and achieve their full potential.

Innovation, a commitment to engineering excellence and leadership development places GE Aerospace based in Cheltenham as a pioneering force in building the future of flight.

Dowty, a GE Aerospace company , is based in Gloucestershire. It is a world-leading supplier of electronically controlled, composite propeller systems for A wide range of civil and military applications, including commercial airliners and military airlifters to multi-role seaplanes and marine hovercraft.

Key programs include the Lockheed Martin C-130J, the De-Haviland, Dash 8-400 and the Leonardo C-27J.

Operated by a highly skilled workforce, Dowty’s’ in-house production expertise for composite blades includes application of resin transfer moulding processes, which have been continuously evolved and perfected since 1976; and the use of braiding machines that rapidly and accurately apply the blades’ fibre outer layers.

If you are passionate about Programme Management, we would like to hear from you.

Qualifications/Requirements

- Currently studying a Business Administration/ Project Management/ Finance/ Data/ Engineering or Program Management related Bachelor’s or integrated   Master’s degree

- On course to achieve a 2:1 degree or above

- To be in your penultimate year of study and returning to education post placement

Desired Characteristics

- Able to roll up your sleeves and get involved in projects

- Organised & able to work towards deadlines

- Inspired and curious to learn

- Strong verbal and written communication skills

- Able to take ownership for projects

- Analytical and problem-solving skills

- Proficient in Microsoft Office

- Able to work as part of a team

A placement at GE Aerospace is an opportunity to learn while doing. At GE Aerospace, you’ll work with business leaders in an atmosphere that will develop you, while doing work that makes an immediate impact.

Total Reward

At GE Aerospace we understand the importance of Total Reward. Our flexible benefits plan, called FlexChoice, gives you freedom, choice, and flexibility in the way you receive your benefits, as well as giving you the opportunity to make savings where possible.

As a new joiner to GE, we are pleased to be able to offer you the following as default in your benefit fund, which you then can tailor to meet your individual needs.

- Non-contributory Pension

- Life Assurance

- Group income protection

- Private medical cover

- Holiday Hourly equivalent of 26 days, with flexible   options   to buy or sell

Recruitment Process

As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to submit an initial CV application. After this, the stages include a video interview, testing and MS Teams online interview. Our recruitment team will be in touch with you at every stage to keep you updated and understand what is next in the process.

If you require any adjustments to the process to enable you to be at your best, please email the team via   UKEarly.Careers@geaerospace.com .

Please note our applications will close on   Saturday 31 st   O ctober   but may close earlier dependant on application volumes. We would encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

Please only submit one application. If you submit multiple applications, we will progress the most suitable one. If in future you are deemed to be suitable for other opportunities, we will automatically consider you for these too.

Security Clearance

Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national   security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance:   BPSS .

Right to Work

Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post.

Further, sponsorship is not available for our Early Careers opportunities. Our placement roles are pipeline for our graduate roles so you would need the permanent right to work to be eligible. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

Whether we are manufacturing components for our engines, driving innovation in fuel and noise reduction, or unlocking new opportunities to grow and deliver more productivity, our GE Aerospace teams are dedicated and making a global impact. Join us and help move the aerospace industry forward.

jobs.title: Power Generation Compliance & Business Operations Leader
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

Job Description
Summary:
The Power Generation Site Compliance Leader & Business Operations Leader is a dual-role position responsible for strengthening the compliance culture and managing compliance risk across the Vandalia and EPISCenter sites, while also driving operational excellence across the Power Generation business. This leader serves as the primary point of contact for site-level compliance matters, partnering closely with site leadership, Site HR, and the Electric Power & Propulsion Compliance Leader to promote a culture of integrity, ethical behavior, and proactive risk identification and mitigation.
In addition, this role drives end-to-end business operations excellence for the Power Generation business, enabling safe, high-quality, on-time, and cost-effective delivery across the Vandalia and EPISCenter sites. The leader will accelerate FLIGHT DECK, develop and sustain cross-site standard work, lead structured problem solving and special projects, standardize operating cadences and escalation forums, aggregate and analyze cross-site performance data, and provide functional leadership in support of MES implementation and business operations integration. This role will report to the Power Generation Operations leader, with dotted line reporting to the Business Unit Leader.
Responsibilities:
Compliance Leader:
- Serve as the on-site compliance expert, advising management and employees on compliance policies and best practices.

- Develop, implement, and monitor site-specific compliance programs, policies, and procedures (Site Compliance Risk Management, Annual Risk Assessment).

- Prepare for leader site visits and round tables.

- Maintain visual compliance across the site (e.g. posters, monthly compliance updates).

- Monitor and deliver compliance-related training programs to all site personnel and new employees.

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date metrics on compliance-related activities.

- Stay informed on GE Aerospace compliance policies and procedures; share and communicate to all site employees.

- Collaborate with GE Aerospace risk owners (e.g. EHS, Security, Quality)

- Serve as intake point for Open Reporting concerns.

Business Ops Leader:
- Standardize operating cadences and escalation forums
- Define and institutionalize cross-site cadences with clear inputs/outputs, owners, and decision logs.

- Lead daily/weekly operating rhythm, tiered meetings, KPI reviews, and standardized escalation paths across sites.

- FLIGHT DECK acceleration and lean transformation
- Facilitate acceleration of lean practices in alignment with enterprise standards; drive maturity of problem solving, visual management, and leader standard work.

- Coach teams on daily management, tiered accountability, and kaizen to stabilize and improve processes.

- Cross-site standard work and problem solving
- Develop, deploy, and maintain standard work across sites for areas such as planning, materials, production control, and change management.

- Lead special projects and structured problem-solving across sites to eliminate systemic constraints and reduce variation.

- Data aggregation and analytics
- Aggregate and analyze cross-site KPIs and leading indicators for WORs, MORs, IOIs, etc.

- Build and maintain dashboards with common definitions and data governance; enable decision-making and proactive risk mitigation.

- New MES implementation leadership (cross-site)
- Provide cross-site functional leadership for MES deployment: define business requirements, standardize processes to be digitized, align data models/BOM-routings, and own cutover readiness criteria.

- Coordinate pilots, change management, user acceptance testing, and training; ensure integration with ERP/MRP and quality systems.

- Track stabilization metrics post-go-live (transaction accuracy, throughput impact, data latency, exception rates).

Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, operations, or related discipline; or equivalent experience.

- 10+ years in supply chain/manufacturing/program leadership in complex, regulated industries (aerospace/defense or electrical systems preferred).

- Ability to handle sensitive issues and conflicts effectively and professionally.

- Demonstrated Respect for People. Strong ethical principles and be well respected among peers.

- Respect and maintain confidentiality on sensitive matters.

- Demonstrated results improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost across multiple sites or value streams.

- Strong ERP/MRP proficiency and experience with demand/capacity planning, SIOP, and data governance.

- Proven lean problem-solving (RCCA), facilitation of cross-functional forums, and standard work deployment.

- Experience leading or supporting MES/industrial digitization initiatives.

This role requires access to U.S. export-controlled information. Therefore, employment will be contingent upon the ability to prove that you meet the status of a U.S. Person as one of the following: U.S. lawful permanent resident, U.S. Citizen, have been granted asylee or refugee status (i.e., a protected individual under the Immigration and Naturalization Act, 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)).

jobs.title: Sr Finance Manager 3 - Product Cost
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Senior Cost Analyst plays a critical role in building and maintaining robust costing processes supporting GE Aerospace supply chain operations. In this role, the Senior Cost Analyst partners with Finance, Manufacturing, and Engineering teams to streamline part cost accumulation and reporting. The role ensures timely, accurate, and complete cost flow and insights to support inventory valuation, operational performance reporting, and effective decision-making for assigned shops.

Job Description
Key Responsibilities
- Review and oversee shop-level costing activities for assigned supply chain shops to ensure accurate and complete costing in line with inventory costing practices.
- Research inventory valuation swings and cost movements; identify drivers and communicate clear, actionable explanations to impacted finance managers and stakeholders.
- Provide ongoing monthly support to shop finance teams by connecting shop operating results to underlying cost and inventory transactions, answering questions on performance and valuation outcomes, and troubleshooting issues by leveraging strong system knowledge and end-to-end understanding of how data flows through costing and inventory processes.
- Monitor inventory balance activity within the cost management system for issues such as negative inventory values; partner with stakeholders to ensure transactions are properly recorded and resolved.
- Support year-end baseline setting activities for assigned shops, establishing expected part costs used to measure operational performance in the following year.
- Support annual physical inventory processes for assigned shops, including periodic site travel as required.
- Collaborate cross-functionally to drive issue resolution, improve data quality, and sustain effective standard work around costing processes.
- Maintain documentation, reconciliations, and communications to support consistent execution and audit readiness.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field (or equivalent experience) with a strong cost accounting foundation.
- 3-5 years of cost accounting experience, preferably in a manufacturing/supply chain environment.
- Advanced Excel skills and strong analytical/problem-solving capability.
- Ability to communicate complex costing topics clearly to finance and non-finance stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with Oracle-based ERPs and/or other inventory/costing systems.
- Experience supporting physical inventory, baseline/standard cost setting, and month-end close activities.
